Check.description: One check and what it found.

advisories.description: Things seen that the contract only recommends against (stderr output that carries no error or result). They never change the result.

findings.description: Everything a `fail` or `unprovided` check found, whole and in order: `reason` is the first three messages, cut.

notRun.description: The commands the fixture names under `notRun`: the checker never ran them, so this check, which runs commands, did not run them either. Information only: it never changes the result, and a command left out of the run is always on the report.

notes.description: Facts the check found that do not change its result: the rules an `entailed` check rests on, a verified Unicode-version difference between the two regular-expression engines.

observed.description: The invocations the verdict rests on: argv, exit, and what the binary printed.

ran.description: How far a check that judges part of its rule without `--deep` ran: `interface` (the part an interface run judges) or `all` (a deep run). Absent for a check that is the same in both modes.

reason.description: Why the check failed, or which fixture entry it lacks.

rules.description: The numbers of the contract's rules the check enforces.

skipped.description: The runs of those commands that this check did not make, each `<command>: <what>: notRun`: runs that would succeed and so never end.

unlisted.description: The write and destructive commands of the tool's documents that no fixture entry covers, named by `L1.constraints`, `L1.domains` and `L1.validators`: the checker never runs them, so they are outside what those checks probe (contract 1.1.2). Information only: it never changes the result.

CheckReport.description: The run: the claimed level, the mode, whether it is passed, and every check.

contractVersion.description: The contract minor the tool claimed and the checks judged.

declaredContractVersion.description: The minor the fixture declares, when `--contract` asked for another one (a preview, never a level claim).

deepChecks.description: The checks of the level that this run did not run, because only `--deep` does (interface mode only), by id.

passed.description: Whether no MUST check of the checks run failed or is unprovided. In interface mode that is a verdict on those checks only, not on the level.

prepare.description: The programs the fixture's `prepare` ran before `setup`, each as its argv: what was made outside the tool, for whoever reviews the claim.

statement.description: `declared X, checked as Y, not a level claim` for a preview.

verdict.description: `preview` when `--contract` differs from the declared minor: the verdict that replaces met and failed. `passed` then only counts the MUST checks.

CheckReport.title: Report

CheckResult.description: The five results of a check (approaches/checker.md 2).

oneOf.description: Exercised and violated; for a SHOULD check, an advisory.
The check needs a fixture entry the tool did not provide.
The check does not apply: no envelope the run saw carries what it judges (`L0.next` without a `meta.next`, `L0.page` without a `meta.page`).
The rule cannot be violated alone (an L1 matter: no L0 check is ever `entailed`).

Detail.description:
One thing a check found, as `data.checks[].findings[]` lists it (approaches/checker.md 2). `kind` is the name of the
condition the check judges, or one of `missing-fixture-entry`, `refused-precondition`, `ran-over-time-limit`; it is
public spelling of the report.

argv.description: The argv of the invocation the finding comes from, when one invocation decided it.

code.description: The registered error code the finding rests on (`refused-precondition`).

Mode.description:
How much of the contract a run checks (approaches/checker.md 3.1). `Interface` is the default: the checks that judge what the tool
prints for ordinary calls, a few process launches on one shared copy of the fixture state. `Deep` (`--deep`) runs every check of the
level, each invocation in a fresh copy of the state.

Strength.description: Whether a failure of the check fails the level.

oneOf.description: A failure, or a missing fixture entry, fails the level.
A failure is an advisory, reported and never failing.

SchemaAnswer.description: One answer of `atip schema`, told apart by `kind`: the tree, a group, a command document, the schemas of a command, the error registry or one entry, the warning registry or one entry (spec 9).
